tldr: An exact two-type residual benchmark yields saturated simultaneous factorial bands under one pooled complete assignment, with fixed potential outcomes and bounded replication. The central Gaussian-CDF error is \(O(\sqrt{\log N/N})\), uniformly over arbitrary unknown arm offsets and \(\epsilon\in[0,1]\), including singular covariance. The translated-cell proof now gives the selected-pair comparison through the explicit cap \(\lfloor\log N/(256\log2)\rfloor\); an explicit smaller logarithmic range has uniformly vanishing relative error. The central proof retains its separate \(\ell_N\) Bonferroni truncation. A common-loading lattice family matches the central rate within the subclass and also gives an obstruction in the broader published complete-randomization framework. Exact Gaussian bands and a finite certified integration and quantile procedure follow. Prospective FrF2 use requires this residual model and pooled global randomization.
